To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we identified novel genome polymorphisms and virulence factor differences among BCG strains.

we identified six large sequence polymorphims among BCG vaccine strains that affect major virulence factors, and that these polymorphisms are likely to be responsible for the differences in adverse effect profile, reactivity to tuberculin and protective efficacy among different BCG vaccines.
the global distribution and propagation of the BCG vaccine strain has contributed to the evolution of the vaccine and is thought to account for the different efficacy outcomes of BCG trials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new vaccines against tuberculosis and other infectious diseases.
understanding the mechanisms of BCG vaccine efficacy.
the molecular mechanisms that underlie differences among BCG strains.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the BCG strains currently used in vaccine trials are not identical.
BCG strains are not all alike and that the genetic diversity among these vaccine strains is a significant factor in the outcome of BCG trials.
the genome of BCG vaccine strains is not static and is constantly changing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BCG is a complex organism with a complex genome and the genome is evolving over time.
the BCG strains have undergone significant genetic alterations during the past 100 years, which have contributed to the phenotypes of the BCG strains.
BCG strains differ from one another in the number of genes that are involved in the virulence and pathogenesis, and the number of virulence genes is associated with the efficacy of BCG vaccine.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is considerable diversity in the genome of the currently used BCG vaccine strain, and that this diversity may be contributing to the variable protective efficacy and adverse effects observed with the vaccine.
the current BCG vaccine strain is highly variable, and this variability has a significant impact on vaccine efficacy and the ability to induce adverse effects.
BCG is not a monolithic entity but is a diverse group of strains with different genetic makeups.
